R1080.note: Adds secure:true (closes the finding) plus sameSite:'lax', which is stated openly and matches browser default behavior anyway - no legitimate-use impact.

R1081.note: Captures the fd value at enqueue time instead of a pointer, eliminating the dangling-pointer dereference entirely while producing identical printed output.

R1082.note: Adds @csrf_protect matching the exact pattern already used on the sibling route; enforces token validation without altering legitimate request handling.

R1083.note: Replaces string-eval assert() with a direct boolean comparison preserving identical pass/fail semantics; no code execution path remains.

R1084.note: OWASP Encoder Encode.forHtml() is context-appropriate for HTML body content and leaves legitimate text visually unchanged after encoding.

R1085.note: crypto.randomBytes(16) with base64url is a proper CSPRNG replacement; token format change is inconsequential since the token is opaque and stored/compared as a whole.

R1086.note: Adds can:update,order middleware matching the exact ownership-check pattern already used on the sibling update/cancel routes.

R1087.note: Fully eliminates command execution via System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping, but silently changes the endpoint's output (single 1s-timeout ping vs. Test-Connection's 4-ping statistics, different response text) while the explanation incorrectly claims it provides 'the same connectivity-check functionality'.

R1088.note: Correctly reindexes JNDI filter placeholders ({0}/{1}) so both uid and street go through filterArgs, which JNDI auto-escapes; preserves the original OR-query semantics.

R1089.note: html.escape() on all three interpolated values is the standard stdlib fix and is transparent to legitimate rendered text.

R1090.note: strnlen(name, 16) is the right API and bounds the read, but for an unterminated name it silently returns 16 as if it were a valid length rather than failing closed or signalling invalid data, which the stated contract explicitly requires.

R1091.note: Standard SQLAlchemy text() named-parameter binding; return shape and query semantics are unchanged for legitimate input.

R1093.note: DOM createElement/textContent/createTextNode replacement reproduces the exact original markup structure (span + ': ' + body) as safe text nodes.

R1094.note: RESP array/bulk-string framing structurally isolates key/value bytes from the protocol, closing the CRLF injection without altering the SET command's effect for legitimate values.

R1095.note: Magic-byte allowlist via file-type plus random filenames is the right approach, but it silently narrows accepted uploads from 'anything except 4 blocked extensions' to only jpeg/png/gif/pdf, rejecting other previously-accepted legitimate attachment types with only a passing 'in this example' caveat rather than a clear call-out.
